title: Integrating Chat-GPT in the Classroom: A Study on Linear Algebra Learning in Higher Education
venue: International Journal of Information and Education Technology
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether and how Chat-GPT can support linear algebra learning in higher education. The authors ask two questions: whether students’ mathematical performance differs across instruction conditions using Chat-GPT versus conventional teaching, and how students perceive Chat-GPT as a learning tool. The study is motivated by the challenge of learning abstract linear algebra concepts and by the growing interest in AI tools for education.

The intervention was evaluated using a mixed-methods design. Quantitatively, the study compared three groups of mathematics education students aged 20–23 from three Indonesian universities: a group taught only with Chat-GPT, a group taught with Chat-GPT plus an expert mathematics educator, and a conventional instruction control group. A post-test and one-way ANOVA were used, and the paper also included a meta-analysis of 19 prior studies on technology and algebra achievement. Qualitatively, five students who experienced the Chat-GPT-supported classes were interviewed using hermeneutic phenomenology to explore their perceptions.

The results showed that the Chat-GPT-plus-instructor condition produced the highest achievement, outperforming both Chat-GPT alone and conventional teaching. Chat-GPT alone did not outperform traditional instruction, suggesting that the tool is most effective when guided by an educator. The meta-analysis found a moderate overall positive effect of technology on algebra achievement, with Chat-GPT-like multimedia showing the strongest moderator effect. Students generally reported that Chat-GPT helped them understand concepts, receive step-by-step explanations, and learn more flexibly, but they also noted that it sometimes made errors and needed human verification. The authors conclude that Chat-GPT should complement rather than replace teachers, especially for more abstract mathematical ideas.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods paper with a small quasi-experimental component, a meta-analysis of prior studies, and qualitative interviews. Because the focal evidence presented here is not a standalone well-controlled RCT and the design includes substantial heterogeneity and interpretive components, the overall evidence quality is best rated yellow despite the included meta-analytic element.
impact_tier_rationale: The meta-analysis reports a moderate pooled effect size (g=0.56, 95% CI [0.40, 0.72]) for technology interventions on algebra achievement, and the Chat-GPT+instructor condition shows a large practical advantage over the comparison groups. This meets the threshold for a medium-or-larger impact on the studied population, even though the Chat-GPT-specific evidence is context-dependent.

interventions.use_case: Chat-GPT 3.5 used as a conversational math tutor for linear algebra problem solving, step-by-step explanations, immediate feedback, and concept support; in one condition it was used alone and in another alongside an expert mathematics educator.

finding.finding_summary: A quasi-experimental ANOVA found significant differences in post-test linear algebra performance across groups (n=30; F=9.745, p=0.001). The Chat-GPT + instructor group scored highest (M=87.58, SD=7.84), Chat-GPT alone scored lowest (M=53.25, SD=22.97), and conventional instruction was intermediate (M=68.40, SD=20.39); Tukey tests showed Chat-GPT + instructor outperformed both other groups, while Chat-GPT alone did not differ significantly from conventional instruction.
finding.measure: Linear algebra post-test scores; one-way ANOVA and Tukey HSD comparisons
finding.std_deviation: Chat-GPT alone SD=22.97; Chat-GPT+instructor SD=7.84; control SD=20.39

finding.finding_summary: Student perceptions were strongly favorable: 36.84% agreed and 57.89% strongly agreed that Chat-GPT helped them understand mathematical concepts better, while 26.32% agreed and 73.68% strongly agreed that it increased interest in learning. The qualitative interviews also suggested reduced anxiety and a more comfortable, non-judgmental learning environment when students could ask repeated questions freely.
finding.measure: Perception questionnaire and semi-structured interview themes on interest, engagement, and comfort

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that Chat-GPT supported step-by-step reasoning, error detection, and conceptual explanation, which students said helped them understand why procedures worked. However, the study also notes a risk of reduced independent thinking if students rely on Chat-GPT for quick answers, making the overall durable-skills effect conditional rather than uniformly positive.
finding.measure: Interview themes on conceptual understanding, reasoning, and independent problem solving

finding.finding_summary: The authors argue that Chat-GPT can provide quick responses, immediate feedback, and 24/7 access to explanations, which may reduce the time students spend waiting for help and support self-paced learning. This is presented as a practical efficiency benefit rather than a separately quantified outcome, with no direct effect size reported.
finding.measure: Interview and questionnaire perceptions of accessibility, immediacy, and ease of use
